* Preamble
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: preamble
:END:

This document formalizes the TMNL (Terminal & Multi-Modal Navigation Layer) system
design, operational protocols, and agent orchestration. It serves as:

1. *Specification* — V-model decomposition of system requirements
2. *Reference* — MCP tool inventory and invocation patterns
3. *Runbook* — Standard Operating Procedures for common workflows
4. *Configuration* — Literate, tangleable definitions for agents, commands, skills, hooks

#+begin_quote
"The map is not the territory, but a good map makes the territory navigable."
#+end_quote

** Document Conventions

| Symbol | Meaning                          |
|--------+----------------------------------|
| ~:tangle~ | Block tangles to specified file  |
| ~:noweb~  | Block uses noweb reference syntax |
| ~SOP~     | Standard Operating Procedure     |
| ~BP~      | Business Process                 |
| ~MCP~     | Model Context Protocol           |

* V-Model Decomposition
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: v-model
:END:

The V-model maps requirements (left arm) to validation (right arm) through
a decomposition hierarchy:

#+begin_example
    REQUIREMENTS                              VALIDATION
    ────────────                              ──────────

    Epic (Strategic)  ◄─────────────────────► System Test
         │                                         ▲
         ▼                                         │
    Feature (Tactical) ◄────────────────────► Integration Test
         │                                         ▲
         ▼                                         │
    Task (Operational) ◄────────────────────► Unit Test
         │                                         ▲
         └──────────► IMPLEMENTATION ─────────────┘
#+end_example

** Hierarchy Semantics

*** Epic (Requirements Level)
- Strategic scope: entire subsystem or capability area
- Acceptance: system-level behavior validation
- Lifecycle: spans multiple sprints/iterations
- Beads type: ~--type=epic~

*** Feature (System Design Level)
- Tactical scope: coherent functional unit
- Acceptance: integration tests across components
- Lifecycle: single sprint deliverable
- Beads type: ~--type=feature~
- Dependency: ~bd dep add <feature> <epic> --type parent-child~

*** Task (Module Design Level)
- Operational scope: atomic, testable unit of work
- Acceptance: unit tests, type checks, lint passes
- Lifecycle: hours to days
- Beads type: ~--type=task~
- Dependency: ~bd dep add <task> <feature> --type parent-child~

* MCP Tool Inventory
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: mcp-inventory
:END:

Model Context Protocol servers extend Claude Code with specialized capabilities.
This section documents all configured MCPs, their tool signatures, and invocation patterns.

** Beads (Issue Tracking)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: mcp-beads
:END:

Local CLI-based distributed issue tracking. Not an MCP server, but integrated
via Bash tool invocations.

*** Tool: ~bd create~

Create a new issue in the beads database.

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd create --title="<title>" --type=<epic|feature|task|bug> --priority=<0-3> --description="<desc>" --json
#+end_src

| Parameter     | Required | Values                    | Description                |
|---------------+----------+---------------------------+----------------------------|
| ~--title~     | Yes      | string                    | Issue title                |
| ~--type~      | No       | epic/feature/task/bug     | Issue classification       |
| ~--priority~  | No       | 0-3 (0=highest)           | Urgency ranking            |
| ~--description~ | No     | string                    | Detailed description       |
| ~--json~      | No       | flag                      | Output as JSON             |

*Example — Create Epic:*
#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd create --title="Data Grid System" --type=epic --priority=1 \
  --description="AG-Grid v34 integration: TmnlDataGrid, theme variants, cell renderers" --json
#+end_src

*** Tool: ~bd dep add~

Wire parent-child or blocking dependencies between issues.

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd dep add <child-id> <parent-id> --type parent-child
bd dep add <blocked-id> <blocker-id>
#+end_src

| Parameter     | Required | Description                              |
|---------------+----------+------------------------------------------|
| ~<child-id>~  | Yes      | Issue that depends on parent             |
| ~<parent-id>~ | Yes      | Issue that child belongs to              |
| ~--type~      | No       | "parent-child" for hierarchy, omit for blocking |

*** Tool: ~bd update~

Modify issue status, assignee, or metadata.

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd update <id> --status=<open|in_progress|closed> --assignee=<username>
#+end_src

*** Tool: ~bd list~

Query issues with filters.

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd list --type=<type> --status=<status> --json
bd ready                    # Show unblocked issues
bd blocked                  # Show blocked issues
#+end_src

*** Tool: ~bd sync~

Synchronize local beads database with git remote.

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
bd sync                     # Full sync
bd sync --status            # Check sync status only
#+end_src

* Standard Operating Procedures
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: sops
:END:

** SOP-001: Session Initialization
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: sop-001
:END:

#+begin_example
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  SESSION INITIALIZATION                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  1. Hook fires: SessionStart:compact                         │
│     └─► Loads beads context, EDIN briefing                  │
│                                                              │
│  2. Run: bd prime (if .beads/ detected)                     │
│     └─► Recovers beads state post-compaction                │
│                                                              │
│  3. Run: bd ready                                            │
│     └─► Shows available work (no blockers)                  │
│                                                              │
│  4. Run: bd stats                                            │
│     └─► Project health overview                             │
│                                                              │
│  5. Review: git status                                       │
│     └─► Understand working tree state                       │
│                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#+end_example

** SOP-002: Task Claim & Execution
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: sop-002
:END:

#+begin_example
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASK EXECUTION                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  1. SELECT WORK                                              │
│     bd ready                                                 │
│     bd show <id>          # Review details + hierarchy      │
│                                                              │
│  2. CLAIM TASK                                               │
│     bd update <id> --status=in_progress                     │
│                                                              │
│  3. EXECUTE                                                  │
│     ├─► Read relevant files                                 │
│     ├─► Implement changes                                   │
│     ├─► Run tests: bun test                                 │
│     └─► Run typecheck: bun typecheck                        │
│                                                              │
│  4. CLOSE                                                    │
│     bd close <id>                                            │
│     # Or with reason:                                        │
│     bd close <id> --reason="Implemented in PR #42"          │
│                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#+end_example

** SOP-003: Session Close Protocol
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: sop-003
:END:

*CRITICAL: Never skip. Work is not done until pushed.*

#+begin_example
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 1. git status           # Check what changed           │
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 2. git add <files>      # Stage code changes           │
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 3. bd sync              # Commit beads changes         │
│         └─► If sync fails, manually:                        │
│             git add .beads/                                  │
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 4. git commit -m "..."  # Commit with message          │
│         └─► Format: <type>(<scope>): <description>          │
│         └─► Include co-author trailer                       │
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 5. bd sync              # Commit any new beads changes │
│                                                              │
│  [ ] 6. git push             # Push to remote               │
│                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#+end_example

** SOP-004: V-Model Decomposition
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: sop-004
:END:

#+begin_example
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               V-MODEL DECOMPOSITION WORKFLOW                 │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  PHASE 1: SUBSYSTEM SCAN                                     │
│  ─────────────────────                                       │
│  Deploy parallel subagents (Task tool) to scan each         │
│  subsystem. Each agent:                                      │
│   • Inventories files (status: COMPLETE/PARTIAL/STUB)       │
│   • Identifies test coverage gaps                           │
│   • Proposes tasks with acceptance criteria                 │
│                                                              │
│  PHASE 2: EPIC CREATION                                      │
│  ──────────────────────                                      │
│  For each subsystem:                                         │
│    bd create --title="<Subsystem>" --type=epic --priority=1 │
│                                                              │
│  PHASE 3: FEATURE EXTRACTION                                 │
│  ──────────────────────────                                  │
│  Group related tasks into features:                          │
│    bd create --title="<Feature>" --type=feature             │
│    bd dep add <feature-id> <epic-id> --type parent-child    │
│                                                              │
│  PHASE 4: TASK ATOMIZATION                                   │
│  ─────────────────────────                                   │
│  Create atomic, testable tasks:                              │
│    bd create --title="<Task>" --type=task --priority=<N>    │
│    bd dep add <task-id> <feature-id> --type parent-child    │
│                                                              │
│  PHASE 5: DEPENDENCY WIRING                                  │
│  ─────────────────────────                                   │
│  Wire blocking dependencies (not parent-child):             │
│    bd dep add <blocked> <blocker>                           │
│                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#+end_example

* Agent Definitions
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agents
:END:

Literate configuration for Claude Code subagent types.
Tangle to ~.claude/agents/~ for activation.

** Explore Agent

Fast codebase exploration with Glob/Grep/Read tools.

#+begin_src yaml :tangle .claude/agents/explore.yaml :mkdirp yes
name: Explore
description: |
  Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to
  quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code
  for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase.

  Specify thoroughness: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate
  exploration, "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis.

tools:
  - Glob
  - Grep
  - Read
  - Bash  # For git log, git blame, etc.

prompts:
  quick: |
    Perform a quick search. Use 1-2 Glob or Grep calls max.
    Return results immediately without deep exploration.

  medium: |
    Moderate exploration. Use up to 5 search calls.
    Follow interesting leads but don't exhaustively explore.

  very_thorough: |
    Comprehensive analysis. Use as many calls as needed.
    Explore multiple naming conventions, check related files,
    trace dependencies across the codebase.
#+end_src

** Plan Agent

Software architect for designing implementation plans.

#+begin_src yaml :tangle .claude/agents/plan.yaml :mkdirp yes
name: Plan
description: |
  Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when
  you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step
  plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs.

tools:
  - Glob
  - Grep
  - Read
  - WebSearch
  - WebFetch
  - mcp__deepwiki__ask_question

outputs:
  - Step-by-step implementation plan
  - Critical files list
  - Architectural trade-offs
  - Risk assessment
  - Estimated complexity

constraints:
  - No time estimates (focus on what, not when)
  - Must read existing code before suggesting changes
  - Must identify all affected files
#+end_src

** Beads Decomposition Agent

Specialized agent for V-model issue decomposition.

#+begin_src yaml :tangle .claude/agents/beads-decomp.yaml :mkdirp yes
name: BeadsDecomposition
description: |
  V-model decomposition agent. Scans a subsystem, identifies gaps,
  and proposes beads issues with acceptance criteria.

tools:
  - Glob
  - Grep
  - Read
  - Bash  # For bd commands (if permitted)

workflow:
  1_scan:
    description: Inventory all files in the subsystem
    output: File status matrix (COMPLETE/PARTIAL/STUB)

  2_analyze:
    description: Identify test coverage and documentation gaps
    output: Gap analysis report

  3_propose:
    description: Generate task proposals with acceptance criteria
    output: List of proposed beads issues

output_format: |
  ## Subsystem: <name>

  ### File Status Matrix
  | File | Status | Notes |
  |------|--------|-------|

  ### Gap Analysis
  - Test coverage: X%
  - Documentation: Y%
  - Missing: [list]

  ### Proposed Tasks
  1. **<title>** (P<priority>)
     - Acceptance: <criteria>
     - Files: <affected>
#+end_src

** /decompose — V-Model Decomposition

#+begin_src markdown :tangle .claude/commands/decompose.md :mkdirp yes
# V-Model Decomposition

Decompose a subsystem or feature into beads issues using V-model methodology.

## Usage
/decompose <subsystem-name>
/decompose --scope=full  (entire TMNL system)

## Process
1. Deploy parallel subagents to scan subsystem(s)
2. Collect file status matrices and gap analyses
3. Create Epic (if scope=full or new subsystem)
4. Extract Features from logical groupings
5. Atomize into Tasks with acceptance criteria
6. Wire parent-child dependencies

## Output
- Summary table of created beads
- Dependency graph visualization
- Next steps recommendation
#+end_src

** /ready — Show Available Work

#+begin_src markdown :tangle .claude/commands/ready.md :mkdirp yes
# Show Ready Work

Display beads issues that are ready to work (no blockers).

## Process
1. Run: bd ready
2. Format output as table with priorities
3. Suggest which task to tackle based on:
   - Priority (P0 > P1 > P2 > P3)
   - Dependencies (unblock others first)
   - Context (related to recent work)
#+end_src

** /close-session — Session Close Protocol

#+begin_src markdown :tangle .claude/commands/close-session.md :mkdirp yes
# Session Close Protocol

Execute the mandatory session close checklist.

## Checklist
1. [ ] git status — check what changed
2. [ ] git add <files> — stage code changes
3. [ ] bd sync — commit beads changes
4. [ ] git commit -m "..." — commit code
5. [ ] bd sync — commit any new beads changes
6. [ ] git push — push to remote

## Enforcement
NEVER mark session complete until all items checked.
Work is not done until pushed.
#+end_src

** /sync — Beads + Git Sync

#+begin_src markdown :tangle .claude/commands/sync.md :mkdirp yes
# Sync Beads and Git

Synchronize beads database and push code changes.

## Process
1. Run: bd sync
2. If sync fails:
   - git add .beads/
   - Report worktree error for user investigation
3. Run: git status
4. If uncommitted changes exist:
   - Prompt for commit message
   - git add . && git commit -m "<message>"
5. Run: git push
#+end_src

** effect-patterns — Effect-TS Pattern Lookup

#+begin_src yaml :tangle .claude/skills/effect-patterns.yaml :mkdirp yes
name: effect-patterns
description: |
  Look up canonical Effect-TS patterns from submodule documentation
  and CLAUDE.md examples.

sources:
  - ../../submodules/effect/packages/*/test/*.test.ts
  - ../../submodules/website/
  - CLAUDE.md (Schema Discipline section)
  - .edin/EFFECT_PATTERNS.md

patterns:
  service:
    description: Effect.Service + Layer.succeed
    example: |
      class MyService extends Context.Tag("app/MyService")<
        MyService,
        { readonly doThing: Effect.Effect<void> }
      >() {}

      const MyServiceLive = Layer.succeed(MyService, {
        doThing: Effect.log("done")
      })

  schema:
    description: Schema.TaggedStruct for discriminated unions
    example: |
      const MyEvent = Schema.TaggedStruct("MyEvent", {
        payload: Schema.String
      })
      type MyEvent = typeof MyEvent.Type

  atom:
    description: Atom.runtime for Effect integration
    example: |
      const runtimeAtom = Atom.runtime(Layer.mergeAll(
        ServiceA.Default,
        ServiceB.Default
      ))

      const myAtom = runtimeAtom.atom(
        Effect.gen(function*() {
          const svc = yield* ServiceA
          return yield* svc.getData()
        })
      )
#+end_src

** ag-grid — AG-Grid Integration Patterns

#+begin_src yaml :tangle .claude/skills/ag-grid.yaml :mkdirp yes
name: ag-grid
description: |
  AG-Grid v34 integration patterns for TMNL.

sources:
  - src/components/tldraw/shapes/data-grid-shape.tsx
  - src/components/tldraw/shapes/data-grid-theme.ts
  - src/lib/data-grid/
  - assets/documents/AG_GRID_THEMING_ARCHITECTURE.md

patterns:
  module_registration:
    description: Required for grid rendering
    example: |
      import { ModuleRegistry, AllCommunityModule } from 'ag-grid-community'
      ModuleRegistry.registerModules([AllCommunityModule])

  cell_renderer:
    description: Custom cell renderer component
    example: |
      const MyCellRenderer: React.FC<{ value: string }> = ({ value }) => (
        <span className="font-mono">{value}</span>
      )

      // In columnDefs:
      { field: 'name', cellRenderer: MyCellRenderer }

  theme:
    description: Programmatic theming via themeQuartz
    example: |
      import { themeQuartz } from 'ag-grid-community'

      const myTheme = themeQuartz.withParams({
        backgroundColor: '#1a1a2e',
        foregroundColor: '#c8e4d8',
        // ...
      })

      <AgGridReact theme={myTheme} ... />
#+end_src

* Hooks

Shell commands executed in response to Claude Code events.
Configure in ~.claude/settings.json~.

** Session Start Hook

#+begin_src json :tangle .claude/hooks/session-start.json :mkdirp yes
{
  "event": "session:start",
  "command": "bd prime 2>/dev/null || true",
  "description": "Recover beads state after session start/compaction"
}
#+end_src

** Pre-Commit Hook

#+begin_src json :tangle .claude/hooks/pre-commit.json :mkdirp yes
{
  "event": "git:pre-commit",
  "command": "bd sync --status",
  "description": "Check beads sync status before committing"
}
#+end_src

** Post-Commit Hook

#+begin_src json :tangle .claude/hooks/post-commit.json :mkdirp yes
{
  "event": "git:post-commit",
  "command": "bd sync 2>/dev/null || (git add .beads/ && echo 'Beads staged for next commit')",
  "description": "Auto-sync beads after code commits"
}
#+end_src

#+begin_example
                    ┌─────────────────────┐

                               │

         ▼                     ▼                     ▼
    ┌─────────┐          ┌─────────┐          ┌─────────┐
    │  EPIC   │          │ FEATURE │          │  TASK   │
    │ type=   │          │ type=   │          │ type=   │
    │ epic    │          │ feature │          │ task    │
    └─────────┘          └─────────┘          └─────────┘

** DT-003: When to Use Subagents

#+begin_example
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Is task parallelizable? │
                    └───────────┬─────────────┘
                                │
                    ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                    ▼                       ▼
                   NO                      YES
                    │                       │
                    ▼                       ▼
           Execute directly        Multiple independent
                               ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                               ▼                       ▼
                          Same tool?             Diff tools?
                               │                       │
                               ▼                       ▼
                    Parallel tool calls      Task tool with
                    in single message        multiple agents
                               │                       │
                               ▼                       ▼
                    ┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
                    │ Multiple calls  │    │ subagent_type=  │
                    │ in single       │    │   explore       │
                    │ message block   │    │   plan          │
                    └─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘

** Types

| Type     | Description                                |
|----------+--------------------------------------------|
| feat     | New feature                                |
| fix      | Bug fix                                    |
| docs     | Documentation only                         |
| style    | Formatting, no code change                 |
| refactor | Code restructure, no feature/fix           |
| perf     | Performance improvement                    |
| test     | Adding/updating tests                      |
| chore    | Build, config, tooling                     |

| Scope        | Area                          |
|--------------+-------------------------------|
| tmnl         | General TMNL changes          |
| canvas       | Canvas system                 |
| layer        | Layer system                  |
| animation    | Animation library             |
| data-grid    | AG-Grid integration           |
| streams      | Streams playground            |
| data-manager | Data manager service          |
| modal        | Modal system                  |
| slider       | Slider system                 |
| tauri        | Tauri integration             |
| beads        | Issue tracking                |

** Tangling Instructions

To extract configuration files from this document:

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
# In Emacs:
# M-x org-babel-tangle

# Or via command line (requires emacs):
emacs --batch -l org --eval "(org-babel-tangle-file \"tmnl-sys-design.org\")"
#+end_src

This will create:
- ~.claude/agents/*.yaml~ — Agent definitions
- ~.claude/commands/*.md~ — Slash commands
- ~.claude/skills/*.yaml~ — Skill configurations
- ~.claude/hooks/*.json~ — Hook definitions

** Document Maintenance

This document should be updated when:
1. New MCP servers are added
2. SOPs change
3. New agents/commands/skills/hooks are defined
4. Beads hierarchy changes significantly
